key_insight: A hemispherical leading-edge curvature changes low-Re flat-plate aerodynamics by promoting earlier vortex shedding and stronger near-wall vortical structures, altering unsteady forces across angles of attack.
engineering_relevance: For small UAV or aquatic vehicle surfaces operating at Re = 1000, leading-edge shape can be tuned to trade off lift, drag, and glide efficiency depending on the target angle-of-attack range.
method: 2D numerical simulation of flow over a flat plate with and without leading-edge curvature
Angle-of-attack sweep from 0° to 25° at Re = 1000
Analysis of vortex shedding behavior, force coefficients, and glide ratio
evidence_signal: The abstract reports delayed shedding for the simple flat plate, onset at 5° for the curved plate, and multiple force-frequency components at higher angles of attack.
watch_item: Because the study is two-dimensional and focused on a single low Reynolds number, the results may not fully transfer to finite-span or higher-Re practical designs without validation.
paper_title: Effect of leading edge geometry on aerodynamic performance of a flat plate
